turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. Come in, have a seat. What have you done?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah it's nothing. Twisted my ankle yesterday.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yesterday. How?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Football, Sunday league. Turned on the pitch and, err, just carried on till the end.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Which ankle, and can you walk on it?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Right one, the outer bit. I can walk. It nips, like a two out of ten, when I put weight on it. Bit puffy if you actually look.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right ankle, outer side, since yesterday, pain about two out of ten on weight bearing, a little swelling, and you are walking.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. We lost two one, that's what I'm annoyed about, not this.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Any numbness or pins and needles in the foot?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Toes are fine. Fuss over nothing.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines? And are you taking anything?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergies. I don't do tablets. Had two paracetemol last night, the 500 ones, and that was it. Biotin is my sister's, she takes it for her nails, not me.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): No allergies, no regular medicine, and the biotin is hers. Any illnesses in the family?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm my dad had diabetes in his fifties, type two I think. Mum did not. My other sister's got pressure, high blood pressure, but no sugar. That's the lot.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Father had type two diabetes from his fifties, your mother did not, and one sister has high blood pressure but not diabetes.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about work, the hours, what you eat, training, and alcohol?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I work in a bike shop, err, about forty hours a week, odd Saturday. Diet's mostly cereal and kebabs. I train Tuesday and Thursday and we play Sunday. Three pints on a Friday after work, and I don't smoke.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bike shop, forty hours, cereal and kebabs, training Tuesday and Thursday, match Sunday, three pints Friday, non-smoker. Shoes off, I'll have a look.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Of. You'll see it's fine.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Swelling over the outer right ankle, and a little bruise coming through. I'm pressing the back of the lateral malleolus, the tip, and the medial malleolus.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Bone's fine. Don't, uh, dig in the soft bit, that nips.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tenderness over the ligament, not on the bone. Take four steps over to the door.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Easy. See, I'm walking. Can I train Thursday or not?

[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Four steps, slight limp, but you are weight bearing. Ottawa ankle rules, there is pain around the malleolus, you carried on playing and you can walk now, and there is no bony tenderness at the posterior tip of either malleolus, so no x-ray today. Working impression, a lateral ligament sprain.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Told you it was nothing.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll prescribe ibuprofen, 400 milligrams three times a day with food, for five days, for the pain and the swelling.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Ugh. Fine, if you insist. I'd rather just ignore it.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Rest it, keep it up, ice for twenty minutes a few times a day, and no football until I've reviewed you.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday's training though.

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not on Thursday. I've booked the nurse Thursday morning, half past eight, to check the swelling and re-strap it. Leave the tubigrip on overnight and come in before the shop. And I'll see you back here in two weeks.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Half eight, I'll be late. I'm not coming in two weeks if it's already better.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's booked either way. No x-ray unless it worsens, if you can't put weight on it or the swelling shoots up then we x-ray. We might do a scan if it does not settle by then, and if an x-ray were borderline we'd do that scan, but I'm not ordering either now.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Whatever. It'll be gone tomorrow.

spec.situation: Young player who twisted the ankle yesterday; swelling, can bear weight with pain; doctor applies Ottawa rules aloud, no X-ray unless it worsens; rest and elevation advice.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.text: paracetamol (dose=500 mg, frequency=two tablets once last night, status=discontinued, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Negative finding asked and answered: no pins and needles in the foot/toes were reported ('Toes are fine').
Medication detail missing/inaccurate: patient had taken paracetamol as two 500 mg tablets last night (total 1 g once), not simply '500 mg'.
Doctor advised no football until reviewed, specifically not to attend Thursday training.
